chapter: From Pittsburgh to Maxine Sullivan: management and style
title: How the Carter tour came about and the Decca switch
summary: She was contacted under her management contract; unsure if it coincided with signing at Decca.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: How did that tour come about?
Well I was contacted, and as I said before, by this time I was under management of MCA, and this was their first experience with singers, I suppose. They were more band oriented.

I suppose this corresponded through your shift over to Dec ca Records as well because I think it's in June of '41, you made your first sides with Dec- ca and you stayed with them for a year and a half.

I'm not sure. It might have been. What I'm thinking is that after the Columbia gave up their bureau and their performing artists for variety acts, let's say, that they just shifted the responsibility somewhere else, you know. They just waited to find out a band was going someplace and they would furnish the singer if they needed one. And I don't know whether that
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

coincided with the DecCa arrangement or not. I'm not sure. But I was still being handled by that office, you know. And of course the Gale Agency, I was contacted, MCA was contacted from the Gale Agency and I think that, I'm trying to think, I think Lew Leslie at the time was connected with the Gale Agency. Lew Leslie was a former producer of some of the early shows. You know, "Black Birds" and things like that. And so he was more familiar with the areas where these types of bands would be excepted. And so I had not been exposed to any band arrangement before. I mean, that is, dance bands and tours and things like that. But I think the Gale Agency must have contacted MCA and between the two of them they arranged for me to go on a tour with Benny Carter.

Okay. I've just been looking through the entry under Benny Carter's name and Brian Rust's and it confirms what I have written down in my notes here is that you recorded with Benny Carter on the 1st of April in 1941. So it's possible that the tour which came later in the year followed as a result of the success of that recording session.

It could be. I'm not too sure about that. I really don't know what was happening. I only know that by that time I was no longer under contract with any recording company. So from then on, I mean, I turned up on alot of different little labels, sometimes at the invitation of the band leader or whatever. I was just free lancing.
